security_case_studies.title: CVE-2026-4963: smolagents PythonExecutor Code Injection — Incomplete Sandbox Fix Exposes RCE
security_case_studies.summary: A code injection vulnerability in Hugging Face smolagents version 1.25.0.dev0 affecting functions evaluate_augassign, evaluate_call, and evaluate_with in src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py. An incomplete fix for CVE-2025-9959 allowed attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code through the LocalPythonExecutor component. Multiple sandbox escape variants were discovered by researcher YLChen-007, including augmented assignment dunder bypass, __str__/__repr__ allowlist abuse, and context manager traceback introspection.

exploit_variants.name: Variant 1: Augmented Assignment Dunder Read Bypass
exploit_variants.description: The evaluate_augassign function contains an internal helper get_current_value that reads attribute values via raw getattr() without any dunder check. The set_value function writes attributes via raw setattr() without dunder checks. This allows reading and overwriting __code__ attributes on function objects to inject arbitrary bytecode.
exploit_variants.bypass_path: obj.__code__ += trap (NOT blocked) vs x = obj.__code__ (blocked)
exploit_variants.attack_vector: Define a class with __radd__ to intercept augmented addition, capture code object, construct malicious CodeType, overwrite victim function's __code__, call it.

exploit_variants.name: Variant 2: Direct __code__ Assignment Bypass
exploit_variants.description: set_value in local_python_executor.py writes attributes via raw setattr() with no dunder protection check, allowing direct overwrite of function __code__ attributes.
exploit_variants.bypass_path: obj.__code__ = evil (NOT blocked by set_value, while evaluate_attribute blocks direct reads)
exploit_variants.attack_vector: Construct a malicious CodeType object with RCE bytecode and directly assign it to a function's __code__ attribute.

exploit_variants.name: Variant 3: __str__/__repr__ Allowed Dunder Method Abuse
exploit_variants.description: CVE-2025-9959 introduced ALLOWED_DUNDER_METHODS = ['__init__', '__str__', '__repr__']. The dunder call check in evaluate_call explicitly skips these methods. User-defined __str__ can contain the generator frame escape primitive (gi_frame.f_locals) to mutate authorized_imports and then import dangerous modules. Calling str(evil_instance) triggers the malicious method.
exploit_variants.bypass_path: str() is available in BASE_PYTHON_TOOLS, and __str__ is allowlisted
exploit_variants.attack_vector: Define a class with a malicious __str__ that uses generator frame introspection to add os to authorized_imports, then import os and call os.system(). Just 8 lines of natural-looking Python.

exploit_variants.name: Variant 4: Context Manager Traceback Frame Introspection (evaluate_with)
exploit_variants.description: The evaluate_with function handling context managers (with statements) can be escaped via traceback frame introspection, achieving RCE by accessing generator frame locals within the with block.
exploit_variants.bypass_path: with statement → traceback frame introspection → authorized_imports mutation
exploit_variants.attack_vector: Use a class implementing __enter__ that captures traceback frames, mutates authorized_imports via gi_frame.f_locals, then imports and executes arbitrary modules inside the with block.

security_case_studies.root_cause: LocalPythonExecutor was designed as a best-effort mitigation layer, not a security sandbox. Hugging Face's own documentation states: 'LocalPythonExecutor provides best-effort mitigations only and is not a security boundary. Do not use it to run untrusted code.' Yet smolagents CodeAgent uses LocalPythonExecutor by default. The custom AST-walking interpreter attempted to block dangerous operations via allowlists and dunder checks, but the patch surface was incomplete — multiple independent code paths (augassign, set_value, allowed dunder methods, context manager evaluation) were not covered by the CVE-2025-9959 fix.
smolagents_cve_timeline: CVE-2025-5120 (Jul 2025): Sandbox escape in v1.14.0 via whitelisted module abuse. Fixed in v1.17.0. CVSS 10.0 Critical.
CVE-2025-9959 (Dec 2025): Dunder attribute validation bypass. Fixed in v1.21.0. CVSS 7.6 High (JFrog).
CVE-2025-14931 (Dec 2025): Pickle deserialization RCE. CVSS 10.0 Critical (ZDI-25-1143).
CVE-2026-4963 (Mar 2026): Incomplete fix for CVE-2025-9959 — three sandbox escape variants. No patch available. Hugging Face did not respond.
Additional 2026 advisories: Sandbox escape via Windows nt.system, str.format dunder bypass, random module abuse, Jinja2 SSTI, Jupyter token leak, SSRF in VisitWebpageTool, timeout-based DoS.

real_world_exploitability.attack_chain: Prompt injection → LLM generates exploit code → LocalPythonExecutor executes it → sandbox escape → RCE on host
real_world_exploitability.likelihood: High. Public PoC exploits released. smolagents agents frequently browse the web (VisitWebpageTool), making prompt injection trivial. The exploit payloads use natural Python patterns (class definitions, str(), with statements) that LLMs readily generate.
real_world_exploitability.impact: Full host compromise with the privileges of the process running the agent. Data exfiltration, lateral movement, persistence on the host.
real_world_exploitability.affected_deployments: Any smolagents CodeAgent using default LocalPythonExecutor. Adoption: ~456K PyPI monthly downloads, 26K GitHub stars.

mitigation: Never use LocalPythonExecutor in production. Hugging Face explicitly warns against it.
Use E2B, Blaxel, Modal, or Docker sandboxed executors instead (remote code execution in isolated containers).
If LocalPythonExecutor is unavoidable, run the entire agent process in a Docker container with minimal privileges and no network access.
Apply principle of least privilege to agent processes. Do not run agents as root with broad filesystem access.
Network isolate agent hosts. Restrict outbound connections.
Implement input sanitization and anomaly detection on code generated by LLMs before execution.
Monitor for post-exploitation indicators: unexpected process spawning, anomalous network connections, file system modifications.
Pin smolagents version and watch for security patches. As of June 2026, no patch for CVE-2026-4963 has been released.
security_case_studies.broader_implications: CVE-2026-4963 exemplifies a systemic pattern across the 2025-2026 AI coding tool ecosystem: AI agent frameworks building their own custom sandboxes instead of using proven isolation technologies (containers, VMs, WASM). Every Python-based agent framework with a built-in code executor (smolagents, LangChain's PythonREPL, n8n's python-task-executor, PraisonAI) has disclosed similar sandbox escape CVEs in 2025-2026. The architectural lesson is that AST-level sandboxing is fundamentally insufficient — real security requires OS-level isolation boundaries.
